extensionDescription.message: Shows when your requests go through an intermediary that decrypts them, such as Cloudflare, Akamai or Imperva.
extensionDescription.description: Description of the extension, shown in the add-ons manager.

titleNeutral.message: No request seen in this tab goes through a known intermediary.
titleNeutral.description: Tooltip of the toolbar icon when no request seen in the tab goes through a known provider.

titleNotObserved.message: Site not observed: the extension's access to this site was withdrawn, so it can say nothing about it.
titleNotObserved.description: Tooltip of the toolbar icon when the extension has no access to the site of the tab and saw nothing.

titleIgnored.description: Tooltip of the toolbar icon when the user asked the extension to ignore the site of the tab.

countLevel2One.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 2, blue, when there is one.

countLevel2Many.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 2, blue, when there are several.

countLevel3ProvenOne.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 3, red, when there is one.

countLevel3ProvenMany.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 3, red, when there are several.

countLevel3UnprovenOne.message: Level 3, reading: 1 request, decryption not proven
countLevel3UnprovenOne.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 3, orange, when there is one.

countLevel3UnprovenMany.message: Level 3, reading: $COUNT$ requests, decryption not proven
countLevel3UnprovenMany.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 3, orange, when there are several.

countLevel4ProvenOne.message: Level 4, personal data: 1 request, decryption proven
countLevel4ProvenOne.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 4, red, when there is one.

countLevel4ProvenMany.message: Level 4, personal data: $COUNT$ requests, decryption proven
countLevel4ProvenMany.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 4, red, when there are several.

countLevel4UnprovenOne.message: Level 4, personal data: 1 request, decryption not proven
countLevel4UnprovenOne.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 4, orange, when there is one.

countLevel4UnprovenMany.message: Level 4, personal data: $COUNT$ requests, decryption not proven
countLevel4UnprovenMany.description: Line of the tooltip that counts the requests of the tab at level 4, orange, when there are several.

titleBlue.message: $PROVIDER$ serves public resources of this page: it knows you are visiting it, and when.
titleBlue.description: Line of the tooltip that says what the provider of the most serious request of the tab sees: blue, levels 1 and 2.

titleOrange.message: This page goes through $PROVIDER$, which may see in clear everything it exchanges with the site.
titleOrange.description: Line of the tooltip that says what the provider of the most serious request of the tab sees: orange, levels 3 and 4, decryption not proven.

titleRed.message: $PROVIDER$ sees in clear everything this page exchanges with the site: web addresses, pages, cookies and forms.
titleRed.description: Line of the tooltip that says what the provider of the most serious request of the tab sees: red, levels 3 and 4, decryption proven.

titleSessionProven.message: Cookies or a login token are part of it, and they can be enough to get into your account.
titleSessionProven.description: Line added to the tooltip when the tab saw a request through a provider that carries a cookie of the site or an Authorization header, and the decryption of one such request was proven.

titleSessionUnproven.message: Cookies or a login token would be part of it, and they could be enough to get into your account.
titleSessionUnproven.description: Line added to the tooltip when the tab saw a request through a provider that carries a cookie of the site or an Authorization header, and the decryption of none was proven.

titleAntiBotProven.message: Part of these exchanges comes from its anti-bot protection.
titleAntiBotProven.description: Line added to the tooltip when the tab saw a request of the anti-bot machinery of a provider, and the decryption of one such request was proven. "Its" is the provider named in the line before.

titleAntiBotUnproven.message: Part of these exchanges would come from its anti-bot protection.
titleAntiBotUnproven.description: Line added to the tooltip when the tab saw a request of the anti-bot machinery of a provider, and the decryption of none was proven. "Its" is the provider named in the line before.

titlePartial.message: Partial view: the extension does not have access to every site, so it shows only what it saw.
titlePartial.description: Line added to the tooltip when the extension lacks the access to all sites.

titleMissed.message: Partial view: the extension could not see every request of this page.
titleMissed.description: Line added to the tooltip when the extension got the response of a request whose sending it never saw, or started after the page did.

popupPage.description: Title of the popup section that shows the counts of the displayed page.

popupUnit.description: Unit at the right of a popup section title whose rows count requests.

popupSite.description: Title of the popup section that shows the kept counts of the site, with the date they started: when the site was last cleared, or when the extension started counting for a site never cleared. Also the title of the counts of a site cleared alone in the panel of the map.

popupSitePrivate.description: Title of the popup section that shows the counts of the site in a private window, which live only for the private session. Also the title of the counts of a site in the panel of the map opened from a private window.

popupBrowserPage.description: Shown in place of the site name in the popup when the tab shows a page of the browser, reader view included.

popupUnknownSite.description: Shown in place of the site name in the popup when the tab shows a website whose site the extension does not know.

popupNothingBrowser.message: No site is shown, so there is nothing to count.
popupNothingBrowser.description: Popup notice for a page of the browser, which has no site to count, shown only when the popup shows nothing else of the page.

popupNothingSite.message: No request seen on this site went through a known intermediary.
popupNothingSite.description: Popup notice under the site title when no request of the site went through a known provider.

popupIgnoreSite.description: Popup button that asks to ignore the site shown from now on, which erases its counts. Hidden when the popup shows no site, in a private window, so that no site visited in private enters the list of ignored sites kept on disk, and for a site already ignored.

popupUnignoreSite.description: Popup button that watches the ignored site shown again, at once and without a question, since nothing is lost. Shown only for an ignored site, in a private window too.

popupClearSite.description: Popup button that asks to clear the counts of the site shown and of no other site: its kept counts, or in a private window its counts of the private session. Hidden when the popup shows no site, and for an ignored site, which keeps no count.

popupIgnore.description: Popup button that confirms ignoring the site the popup shows, which erases its counts.

popupClear.description: Popup button that confirms the clearing of the counts of the site the popup shows.

popupCancel.description: Popup button that gives up the clearing of the counts of the site the popup shows, or ignoring it.

popupIgnoreSiteQuestion.description: Question the popup asks before it ignores the site shown, with the site as the popup header shows it. Ignoring a site erases its counts.

popupClearSiteQuestion.message: Clear the counts of $SITE$ kept since $DATE$?
popupClearSiteQuestion.description: Question the popup asks before it clears the kept counts of the site shown, and of no other site, with the site as the popup header shows it and the date its counts started.

popupClearSiteQuestionPrivate.message: Clear the counts of $SITE$ in this private session?
popupClearSiteQuestionPrivate.description: Question the popup of a private window asks before it clears the counts of the site shown in the private session, and nothing of its kept counts nor of the other sites, with the site as the popup header shows it.

popupIgnored.description: Title the popup shows in place of the counts when the user asked to ignore the site shown.

popupIgnoredText.message: Cloud Leak does not look at the requests of this site and counts none of them.
popupIgnoredText.description: Popup text under the title of an ignored site, which says why the popup shows no count.

popupWatchedAgain.message: This site is watched again, from the next load of the page.
popupWatchedAgain.description: Popup text shown right after the user stopped ignoring the site shown: the page still open was not watched meanwhile.

helpOpen.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the question mark in a circle, at the top right of the popup and of the map, which opens the help.

helpTitle.message: The levels and how serious they are
helpTitle.description: Title of the help window of the popup and of the map, which explains the leak levels and how serious each one is.

helpClose.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the cross that closes the help window.

helpRoute.message: When you browse the Internet, absolutely everything you look at, everything you say, and even what is private, goes through a set of computers known as servers.
helpRoute.description: Help, paragraph 1: everything a browser exchanges goes through many computers.

helpHttps.message: When the address starts with “https”, the connection is said to be encrypted. Normally, this means that only you and the site you visit know what happens between you. For instance, when you pay with your card or file your taxes, it is better not to have someone in the middle who could see all that.

helpProviders.message: However, most often for performance or to protect itself from attacks, a site can call on a company that handles part of the processing of the pages you visit. Where these services become a problem is that, to work, they may need to read what you exchange with the site.
helpProviders.description: Help, paragraph 3: the providers that stand between the user and the site, and decrypt the connection.

helpLaw.message: These services can potentially see all your data, yes, even your card number, if the payment site uses one of them. These companies answer to their government, which may be a foreign power to yours. So everything that goes through them is subject to the authorities of their country, on top of yours.
helpLaw.description: Help, paragraph 4: the providers obey the law of their country, which the flag of the map shows.

helpStates.message: It becomes possible for these states to decide whether a site is available, to intercept your information and to use it as they see fit.
helpStates.description: Help, paragraph 5: what the states of the providers can do.

helpLevels.message: This risk can be ranked simply.
helpLevels.description: Help: introduces the list of the levels.

helpLevel2.message: Level 2, public resources are used that go through one of these services, with little at stake.
helpLevel2.description: Help, list of the levels: level 2, named as in the popup.

helpLevel3.message: Level 3, the pages you read go through one of these services.
helpLevel3.description: Help, list of the levels: level 3, named as in the popup.

helpLevel4.message: Level 4, sensitive information goes through one of these services, such as what you send or your sign-in to an account.
helpLevel4.description: Help, list of the levels: level 4, named as in the popup.

helpColours.message: In orange, nothing proves that the service reads what goes through. In red, it is proven, it reads it and can change it.
helpColours.description: Help, last paragraph: what orange and red say of the proof.

popupPreferences.description: Accessible name and tooltip of the gear of the popup, which opens the preferences of the extension in the add-ons manager.

level1.description: Name of leak level 1 in a row of the popup.

level2.description: Name of leak level 2 in a row of the popup and of the panel of the map.

level3.description: Name of leak level 3 in a row of the popup and of the panel of the map.

level4.description: Name of leak level 4 in a row of the popup and of the panel of the map.

decryptionProven.description: Proof line under a red row of the popup and of the panel of the map.

decryptionUnproven.description: Proof line under an orange row of the popup and of the panel of the map.

optionsIgnoredSites.description: Title of the list of ignored sites, the first title of the preferences page.

optionsIgnoredText.message: Cloud Leak does not look at the requests of these sites and counts none of them.
optionsIgnoredText.description: Text under the title of the list of ignored sites in the preferences.

optionsRemove.description: Button of each ignored site in the preferences, which watches the site again at once, without a question, since nothing is lost.

optionsRemoveSite.description: Accessible name of the button that removes an ignored site in the preferences, with the site as the list shows it.

optionsEmpty.message: No site is ignored. Add one below, or click Ignore in the Cloud Leak window.
optionsEmpty.description: Text of the preferences in place of the list when no site is ignored. "Ignore" is the button of the popup, the window the toolbar button opens.

optionsAddSite.description: Label of the field of the preferences where the user types a site to ignore.

optionsAdd.description: Button of the preferences that ignores the site the field names, which erases its counts, without a question.

optionsHelp.message: A domain or an address, reduced to its site (www.twitch.tv gives twitch.tv). Its counts are erased.
optionsHelp.description: Help under the field of the preferences while nothing is typed: what to type, how it is reduced to its registrable domain, and that adding a site erases its counts.

optionsPreview.description: Line under the field of the preferences while the text typed names a site, followed by that site, in bold: what the Add button will ignore.

optionsRefused.message: No site matches “$TEXT$”. Type a domain, such as twitch.tv.
optionsRefused.description: Line under the field of the preferences when the text typed names no site, with that text: nothing is added.

optionsAlready.description: Line under the field of the preferences when the text typed names a site already in the list, with the site as the list shows it.

optionsRecord.description: Title of the section of the preferences, after the ignored sites, that turns on the recording of the reduced addresses of requests, and the name of that option.

optionsRecordText.message: The addresses of the requests of the chosen levels are kept on this computer, without the values of their parameters, and can reveal what you did on a site: when in doubt, leave it on “None”.
optionsRecordText.description: Text under the title of the recording of addresses in the preferences: what is kept, where, what it can reveal, and the advice to keep the choice that records nothing, named as its radio button is.

optionsRecordNone.description: Radio button of the preferences that records no address, the default. In French it agrees with « adresses ».

optionsRecordLevel4.description: Radio button of the preferences that records the addresses of the requests of level 4 only, with the name of the level.

optionsRecordLevel3and4.message: Levels 3 and 4, reading and personal data
optionsRecordLevel3and4.description: Radio button of the preferences that records the addresses of the requests of levels 3 and 4, with the names of the levels.

optionsRecordPrivate.message: Nothing is recorded in a private window.
optionsRecordPrivate.description: Line under the radio buttons of the recording of addresses: whatever the choice, no address of a request of a private window is kept.

optionsRecordQuestion.description: Question the preferences ask, under the radio buttons, when the user goes back to recording no address, which clears every kept address. Nothing changes before the answer.

optionsPurge.description: Button of the preferences that confirms going back to recording no address, which clears every kept address.

optionsCancel.description: Button of the preferences that gives up going back to recording no address, and keeps the choice and the addresses as they were.

optionsRecordPurged.description: Line of the preferences once the user confirmed going back to recording no address and every kept address is cleared.

optionsLimit.description: Label of the field of the preferences that sets how many addresses are kept for each row, shown only while addresses are recorded.

optionsLimitHelp.message: The number of addresses to keep for each site, by request type and by method seen.
optionsLimitHelp.description: Help under the field of the limit in the preferences: what the limit counts, for each site, request type and method.

optionsLimitError.message: Type a whole number of at least 1.
optionsLimitError.description: Line under the field of the limit, in place of its help, when what is typed is not a whole number of at least 1: nothing is kept. The limit has no maximum.

mapTitle.description: Title of the map, in its header and in the title of its tab.

mapKeptSince.description: Subtitle of the map when nothing is kept, with the date the kept counts started.

mapKeptSinceSummary.description: Subtitle of the map, with the date the kept counts started, the number of sites and the number of providers, each as mapSitesOne or mapSitesMany and mapProvidersOne or mapProvidersMany give it.

mapPrivateSession.description: Subtitle of the map opened from a private window when the private session counted nothing.

mapPrivateSessionSummary.description: Subtitle of the map opened from a private window, which shows the counts of the private session only, with the number of sites and of providers.

mapPurgeAll.description: Button of the map that asks to clear the counts of every site: the kept counts, or from a private window those of the private session. Hidden when nothing is kept.

mapPurgeAllQuestion.message: Clear all the counts kept since $DATE$?
mapPurgeAllQuestion.description: Question the map asks before it clears every kept count, with the date they started.

mapPurgeAllQuestionPrivate.message: Clear all the counts of this private session?
mapPurgeAllQuestionPrivate.description: Question the map opened from a private window asks before it clears the counts of the private session, and nothing of the kept counts.

mapPurge.description: Button of the map that confirms the clearing of the counts of every site.

mapCancel.description: Button of the map that gives up the clearing of the counts of every site.

mapNothingKept.description: Shown in place of the map when no request went through a provider since the kept counts started, with that date.

mapNothingPrivate.message: No counts in this private session.
mapNothingPrivate.description: Shown in place of the map opened from a private window when the private session counted nothing.

mapLegendRed4.description: Legend of the map: the link of level 4, decryption proven, red, thick and solid.

mapLegendRed3.description: Legend of the map: the link of level 3, decryption proven, red and solid.

mapLegendOrange4.description: Legend of the map: the link of level 4, decryption not proven, orange, thick and dashed.

mapLegendOrange3.description: Legend of the map: the link of level 3, decryption not proven, orange and dashed.

mapLegendBlue2.description: Legend of the map: the link of level 2, blue, thin and solid.

mapLegendSite.message: site, by its most serious request
mapLegendSite.description: Legend of the map, after a red cloud, an orange cloud and a blue point: how a site is drawn.

mapLegendProvider.message: provider, flag of the applicable law
mapLegendProvider.description: Legend of the map, after a flag: the flag of a provider is the country whose law the service is subject to.

mapLegendScope.message: Without private windows or ignored sites.
mapLegendScope.description: End of the legend of the map: what its counts leave out.

mapLegendScopePrivate.message: This private session only, without ignored sites.
mapLegendScopePrivate.description: End of the legend of the map opened from a private window: what its counts hold and leave out.

mapSearch.description: Placeholder and accessible name of the field of the map that keeps the sites whose name holds what is typed.

mapCategoryRed4.description: Name of the limit of the map to the links of level 4, decryption proven, on its chip.

mapCategoryRed3.description: Name of the limit of the map to the links of level 3, decryption proven, on its chip.

mapCategoryOrange4.description: Name of the limit of the map to the links of level 4, decryption not proven, on its chip.

mapCategoryOrange3.description: Name of the limit of the map to the links of level 3, decryption not proven, on its chip.

mapCategoryBlue2.description: Name of the limit of the map to the links of level 2, on its chip.

mapRemoveLimit.description: Accessible name of the cross of a chip of the map, which removes its limit, with the name the chip shows.

mapClearFilters.description: Button of the map that empties the search field and removes every limit at once.

mapNoMatch.description: Shown in place of the column of the map when the search and the limits keep no site.

mapSitesHeading.message: Sites, from the most serious to the least
mapSitesHeading.description: Heading of the column of the sites on the map.

mapUnit.description: Unit at the right of a heading of the map whose numbers count requests.

mapProvidersHeading.description: Heading of the providers on the map, and of the list of the other providers in its panel.

mapHeadingRed4.description: Heading, shown in capitals, of the sites of the map whose most serious request is at level 4, decryption proven.

mapHeadingRed3.description: Heading, shown in capitals, of the sites of the map whose most serious request is at level 3, decryption proven.

mapHeadingOrange4.description: Heading, shown in capitals, of the sites of the map whose most serious request is at level 4, decryption not proven.

mapHeadingOrange3.description: Heading, shown in capitals, of the sites of the map whose most serious request is at level 3, decryption not proven.

mapHeadingBlue2.description: Heading, shown in capitals, of the sites of the map whose most serious request is at level 2.

mapGroupLevel.description: Shown in grey right after the number of sites of a row of the map that gathers the blue sites through the same providers, such as "334 sites".

mapLevelRed4.description: Category of a request in the tooltips of the map, after "at" or "at most".

mapLevelRed3.description: Category of a request in the tooltips of the map, after "at" or "at most".

mapLevelOrange4.message: level 4, personal data, decryption not proven
mapLevelOrange4.description: Category of a request in the tooltips of the map, after "at" or "at most".

mapLevelOrange3.description: Category of a request in the tooltips of the map, after "at" or "at most".

mapLevelBlue2.description: Category of a request in the tooltips of the map, after "at" or "at most".

mapSiteTitle.description: Tooltip of a site on the map, with the site, its number of requests and the category of its most serious request.

mapLinkTitle.description: Tooltip of the link between a site and a provider on the map, with the number of requests of the site through the provider and the category of the most serious one.

mapGroupTitle.description: Tooltip of a row of the map that gathers the blue sites through the same providers, with the number of sites and the names of the providers.

mapGroupLinkTitle.description: Tooltip of the link between a row of gathered blue sites and one of their providers on the map.

mapProviderLaw.description: Tooltip of a provider on the map, with the country whose law the service is subject to, as mapLawOf followed by its code gives it.

mapProviderLawParent.message: $PROVIDER$, subject to the law $LAW$, parent company $PARENT$, $PLACE$
mapProviderLawParent.description: Tooltip of a provider on the map whose parent company is in another country, with the country of the law as mapLawOf gives it, and the country of the parent company as mapIn gives it.

mapLawOfUS.description: The United States, after "subject to the law" in the tooltip of a provider on the map.

mapLawOfFR.description: France, after "subject to the law" in the tooltip of a provider on the map.

mapLawOfIL.description: Israel, after "subject to the law" in the tooltip of a provider on the map.

mapInUS.description: Where the parent company of a provider is, in its tooltip on the map: the United States.

mapInFR.description: Where the parent company of a provider is, in its tooltip on the map: France.

mapInIL.description: Where the parent company of a provider is, in its tooltip on the map: Israel.

mapOverview.description: Title of the panel of the map without a selection, search or limit.

mapShownSites.description: Title of the panel of the map without a selection, under a search or a limit.

mapOverviewLine.description: First line of the panel of the map without a selection: the sites shown, their providers and their requests.

mapOverviewHelp.message: Click a site, a provider or a link for its details.
mapOverviewHelp.description: Help of the panel of the map without a selection.

mapLimitHelp.message: Click a row below to limit the map to its sites, click it again to remove the limit.
mapLimitHelp.description: Help of the panel of the map without a selection, about the rows of its three lists.

mapByLinks.description: Title of the list of categories in the panel of the map, where a site counts in the category of each of its links.

mapSitesUnit.description: Unit at the right of a heading of the panel of the map whose numbers count sites.

mapByLinksNote.message: A site counts in the category of each of its links, so the sum exceeds the number of sites.
mapByLinksNote.description: Note under the list of categories in the panel of the map.

mapByCountry.description: Title of the list of countries in the panel of the map: the countries whose law the providers are subject to.

mapByCountryNote.message: A site counts in the country of each of its providers.
mapByCountryNote.description: Note under the list of countries in the panel of the map.

mapByProvider.description: Title of the list of providers in the panel of the map.

mapBack.description: Button of the panel of a site, a provider or a group of sites on the map, which shows the panel without a selection again.

mapSince.description: Title of the counts of a site, or of a group of sites, in the panel of the map, with the date the kept counts started.

mapOwnDate.message: Cleared alone, this site has its own date.
mapOwnDate.description: Note of the panel of a site on the map whose counts start at its own date, since it was cleared alone or watched again.

mapSubjectTo.description: Line of the panel of a provider on the map, with the name and the flag of the country whose law the service is subject to.

mapParent.description: Line of the panel of a provider on the map whose parent company is in another country, with its name and the name and flag of its country.

mapProviderNote.description: Note of the panel of a provider on the map, with the date the kept counts started.

mapProviderNotePrivate.description: Note of the panel of a provider on the map opened from a private window.

mapByWorst.description: Title of the categories in the panel of a provider on the map, where each site counts in the category of its most serious request through the provider.

mapItsSite.description: Title of the list of sites in the panel of a provider on the map that has one site.

mapItsSites.description: Title of the list of sites in the panel of a provider on the map that has several.

mapGroupText.description: Text of the panel of a group of blue sites on the map, with the names of their providers.

mapThisPrivateSession.description: Title of the counts of a group of sites in the panel of the map opened from a private window.

mapSitesOne.description: A number of sites that takes the singular, on the map.

mapSitesMany.description: A number of sites that takes the plural, on the map.

mapSitesOfOne.description: How many sites the search and the limits keep of a total, on the map, when the first number takes the singular.

mapSitesOfMany.description: How many sites the search and the limits keep of a total, on the map, when the first number takes the plural.

mapProvidersOne.description: A number of providers that takes the singular, on the map.

mapProvidersMany.description: A number of providers that takes the plural, on the map.

mapRequestsOne.description: A number of requests that takes the singular, on the map.

mapRequestsMany.description: A number of requests that takes the plural, on the map.

mapTypeMainFrame.description: Name of the request type main_frame, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeSubFrame.description: Name of the request type sub_frame, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeXmlhttprequest.description: Name of the request type xmlhttprequest, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeScript.description: Name of the request type script, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeImage.description: Name of the request type image, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeStylesheet.description: Name of the request type stylesheet, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeFont.description: Name of the request type font, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeMedia.description: Name of the request type media, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeWebsocket.description: Name of the request type websocket, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapTypeOther.description: Name of the request type other, after its method, in the panel of a site on the map.

mapAddressesOne.message: $COUNT$ address kept. A click copies it.
mapAddressesOne.description: Line under the unfolded list of the kept addresses of a row of the panel of a site, when the list holds a number of addresses that takes the singular, below the limit set in the preferences.

mapAddressesMany.message: $COUNT$ addresses kept. A click copies one.
mapAddressesMany.description: Line under the unfolded list of the kept addresses of a row of the panel of a site, when the list holds a number of addresses that takes the plural, below the limit set in the preferences.

mapAddressesLimitOne.message: $COUNT$ address kept, the limit set in the preferences. A click copies it.
mapAddressesLimitOne.description: Line under the unfolded list of the kept addresses of a row of the panel of a site, when the list holds a number of addresses that takes the singular and has reached the limit set in the preferences, so that the list does not pass for complete.

mapAddressesLimitMany.message: $COUNT$ addresses kept, the limit set in the preferences. A click copies one.
mapAddressesLimitMany.description: Line under the unfolded list of the kept addresses of a row of the panel of a site, when the list holds a number of addresses that takes the plural and has reached the limit set in the preferences, so that the list does not pass for complete.

mapAddressCopied.description: Word of the chip shown for 1.5 seconds, after a check mark, on an address of the panel of a site once a click copied it. In French it agrees with « adresse ».

mapAddressCopyFailed.description: Word of the chip shown for 1.5 seconds on an address of the panel of a site when a click could not copy it, and what a screen reader hears then.

mapAddressCopiedAnnounced.description: What a screen reader hears once a click on an address of the panel of a site copied it.
